- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep decline, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for overshoot.
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, apply a 1–3% upward bias to reflect mean reversion toward recent trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), avoid over-optimistic tail behavior — cap forecast variance at ±3% of recent 7-day range.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., 2+ consecutive sentiment flips), reduce forecast lag by 1–2 days to align with sentiment momentum.
